page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.A2.Flex.2-8 is a flexible compute instance powered by the Ampere AmpereOne (Ampere-1) processor family. It features 4 dedicated 64-bit Arm physical cores operating at a base frequency of 3.0 GHz with single-threaded execution per core. The instance is configured with 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per core. It includes no bundled local NVMe storage and no hardware GPU accelerators, relying on remote network storage volumes for persistence. A single complimentary public IPv4 address is provisioned by default.

Benchmark results place the instance primarily in lower performance tiers relative to broader cloud baselines. In CPU workloads, it recorded a Geekbench multi-core score of 2,858.0 alongside a single-core score of 892.0, while PassMark CPU benchmarks reached 2,891.32. While L1/L2 cached memory access demonstrated an average 349.64 GB/sec bandwidth for small 16 KB blocks, large-block uncached memory operations measured 15.25 GB/sec for reads and 13.13 GB/sec for writes. Workload-specific tests yielded 4.85 million operations per second in Redis SET commands and 5.09 GB/sec throughput for static web serving.

Given its dedicated physical Arm cores and 1:2 core-to-memory density, VM.Standard.A2.Flex.2-8 offers an entry-level compute footprint for cost-sensitive environments. Because there is no onboard storage and raw integer and single-thread throughput are constrained, the instance is best suited for lightweight web frontends, basic microservices, continuous integration build nodes for Arm targets, and development environments rather than memory-heavy or high-throughput database systems.
